findings.problem: LeaseWorkflow uses primitive String status plus separate bool flags (is_validated, is_sent). This allows illegal states such as status="sent" with is_sent=false, or is_sent=true with status="pending". The struct has no invariant enforcement.
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can place the lease in a logically inconsistent state, breaking downstream invariants that assume status and is_sent agree. Bugs are silent — no panic, no error, just wrong state.
findings.fix: Replace status: String and is_validated: bool, is_sent: bool with a single LeaseStage enum typestate (e.g., Pending, Validated, Sent) that encodes all valid lifecycle transitions at the type level.

findings.problem: id is pub String with no domain newtype. Any string (empty, malformed, reused) is accepted as a lease ID.
findings.failure_mode: Empty or duplicate IDs can be constructed freely, causing collision or lookup failures at the boundary where the ID is used.
findings.fix: Introduce a LeaseId newtype with a fallible constructor that rejects empty/invalid IDs. Make the field private or expose via &str only.

findings.problem: status is pub String — freeform text instead of a closed enum. Callers can set arbitrary status strings.
findings.failure_mode: Downstream code matching on literal status strings is fragile; typos silently produce unknown states instead of compile-time errors.
findings.fix: Replace with a LeaseStage enum. Remove the separate is_sent field entirely since sent-ness is derivable from the enum variant.

findings.problem: mark_sent takes ownership of LeaseWorkflow and mutates it in place with string allocation and flag toggling. This is imperative mutation of domain data, not a pure transformation.
findings.failure_mode: The function has no preconditions, no validation, and allocates a new String for every call. It cannot be unit-tested deterministically without heap interaction, and the mutation bypasses any invariant checks.
findings.fix: Define mark_sent as a pure function on the typestate enum: fn stage_transition(LeaseStage) -> Result<LeaseStage, TransitionError>. Move string allocation and I/O to an imperative shell layer that orchestrates transitions.

findings.problem: item.status = "sent".to_string() allocates a new String on every call instead of using an enum or interned representation.
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary heap allocation on every state transition. Combined with the String status field, every write path must allocate.
findings.fix: Replace with an enum variant; no allocation needed for state encoding.

findings.problem: All fields of LeaseWorkflow are pub. There is no constructor, no encapsulation, and no way to enforce invariants.
findings.failure_mode: Any code in the crate or downstream can construct a LeaseWorkflow with arbitrary field combinations, making it impossible to guarantee correctness without runtime checks everywhere.
findings.fix: Make all fields private. Provide a fallible constructor `LeaseWorkflow::new(id: LeaseId) -> Self` that initializes the typestate to the first valid stage.

findings.problem: mark_sent performs allocation (.to_string()) and mutates state as a side effect of what should be a pure domain operation.
findings.failure_mode: Allocation failure (OOM) silently propagates as a panic via .to_string(). The caller has no way to handle the allocation failure gracefully.
findings.fix: Use an enum for state encoding (no allocation). If allocation is truly needed, use try_reserve or return Result with a typed allocation error.
